summary:
Leo is a rapidly scaling, working-capital-heavy food trader, processor and distributor, not yet an evidenced premium branded-consumer compounder. FY26 revenue doubled to INR 174.24 crore while operating EBITDA reached 19.85 crore. The strongest evidence is the increase in retained economic spread as well as turnover. The decisive weakness is cash: FY22-FY26 cumulative CFO was minus 62.92 crore against PAT 29.05 crore, with only 0.1585 crore cash at March 2026. A low-looking historical 10.19x earnings multiple therefore does not establish cheapness.

Classification: high-growth, cash-conversion and recapitalization-dependent special-situation watchlist; no supported ordinary entry or return. BQS, GQS and IAS are NS because CAP, supported R and L remain incomplete, not because the business has been assigned a zero. G2/G3/G4 remain Hold. The counterfactual rescue model is deliberately separate: its base 8.61% return is neither an available deal nor a price target. Proposed 42 crore warrants could change capital capacity, but only 10.5 crore is the minimum deposit if approved/allotted and 31.5 crore depends on optional exercise. Reconciled reliability, current funding and better collection evidence, rather than headline sales alone, would change the conclusion.

sections.text:

The 19 October INR 60 quote is a dated secondary BSE snapshot corroborated by two services, not an independently authenticated official close or executable bid. Market capitalization is 107.35 crore; March-balance enterprise value 144.14 crore.

Horizon is 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031, nominal pretax equity hurdle 15%, with 12%/18% sensitivities. The INR 5 lakh reference position is illustrative, not a recommendation: four lots cost 4.8 lakh and five cost 6 lakh. sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors are GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 2, BAL 3, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R NS, D 3, P 4 and L NS. Every factor has two material facts, counterevidence, confidence and evidence IDs in the embedded audit. REV starts at 9 under the >=30% schedule, with no discretionary trajectory adjustment; the Medium-confidence/short relevant history ceiling makes 8. CAP is not replaced by book ROCE or a neutral 5.

Exact Decimal BQS known contribution is 4.20 at 88% coverage, leaving raw bounds 4.32-5.40. GQS known contribution 5.35 at 85% coverage leaves 5.50-6.85 before the persistent CASH<=3 ceiling of 5. The capped interval is not a scored point while CAP is missing. IAS known contribution 1.00 at 30% coverage leaves 1.70-8.00; its quality input remains NS because final BQS is NS. Weights are unchanged and missing weights are not redistributed. An illustrative CAP score 3 would yield BQS 4.56 and capped GQS 5, but this is judgment sensitivity, not a new canonical estimate. R cannot be derived from a hypothetical rescue return and L cannot be assigned from a one-day volume. No composite ranking or compounder label is supported.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Four different earnings engines must be separated. Commodity trading buys whole spices and dryfruits in bulk and resells them, sometimes unbranded: turnover includes pass-through commodity value, while procurement, spoilage, customer credit and inventory financing determine the retained spread. Processing cleans, grades, grinds, blends and packages products. It earns conversion value, but capacity utilization, yield, batch quality and incremental returns are needed before treating factory sales as a durable advantage. VANDU branded spices/grocery and FRYD frozen products may earn consumer margins, but brand presence is not proof of pricing power or consumer repeat rates. Distribution, including third-party products, earns a narrower access/logistics spread and can consume credit even when capex is light.

In FY24 the prospectus attributed 77.17% of turnover to trading and 22.83% to processing. B2B was 77.18%, B 2 C 16.99% and D 2 C 5.83%; September 2024 B2B rose to 94.8%. These historical shares cannot be relabelled FY26. FY26 reports one operating segment without current brand/channel profitability. Products include whole/blended spices, plain/roasted/flavoured dryfruits, grocery and frozen foods; some branded items are procured externally. APMC proximity can lower sourcing/logistics friction, but no long-term supply/customer contract protects the spread. Institutional and rail/canteen access is an opportunity, not automatically recognized backlog or cash.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Leo's useful capabilities are procurement proximity, cleaning/blending/packing, product breadth and routes to distributors and institutions. Reported 150 distributors,300-plus SKUs and approximately 75% utilization indicate operating infrastructure, but they do not disclose repeat sell-through, price premium, distributor churn, net returns or customer switching costs. Historical geography was concentrated: FY24 Maharashtra 96.71% and top-ten customers 44.29%; the H1FY25 top-ten figure 93.32% demonstrates how channel mix can raise concentration rapidly. Current customer shares are a missing update, not assumed unchanged.

Proventus is a closer business-model comparator because it combines bulk sourcing, processing, white-label and a consumer brand; Madhusudan is relevant for ground/blended spice portfolios and retail/wholesale channels. Sarveshwar is an adjacent rice/organic processor whose aging/export cycle prevents a simple multiple transplant. Primary peer descriptions were read; undated capacity claims were not promoted into current market-share estimates. The IPO prospectus FY24 table shows Leo revenue 62.17 crore and 17.91% EBITDA margin, compared with Madhusudan 162.22 and 10.68%, HOAC 15.63 and 11.63%, and Jetmall 1.31 and 8.38%. These are historic issuer-selected figures, not current peer valuation. Leo's FY26 margin 11.39% has already moved much closer to ordinary processing/distribution economics. MOAT 4 reflects limited evidence of lasting differentiation, not a claim that food demand is weak.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The window was selected before scoring: FY23-FY26 captures three full years after processing began, while the FY22 startup base of 5.27 crore is shown but not used to claim a 139.84% durable growth rate. Revenue 36.44 to 174.24 gives 68.47% CAGR; FY24/FY25/FY26 additions were 25.73,25.15 and 86.93 crore. Retained spread, defined only as revenue less materials/purchases adjusted for inventory, rose from 7.8630 to 30.2381 crore, a 56.67% CAGR. This is a value-added crosscheck, not a brand gross margin, because it excludes payroll, freight, selling and other conversion expenses.

FY26 dryfruit sales increased 64.62 crore and account for 74.33% of the total sales increment. Whole spices added 2.36 crore, blended spices 9.83, other grocery 9.84, packing 0.28, and frozen was broadly flat. The gross-spread percentage fell from 23.69% to 17.35%, while EBITDA margin fell 16.93% to 11.39%; sales doubled but PAT grew 29.09%. This mix and margin evidence argues against describing the year as pure brand-led pricing power. Current quantities, selling realization and segment-acquisition contributions are not separately available. REV 8 is therefore operating-scale expansion corroborated by economic spread, not a measured organic-volume CAGR. No additional small-base penalty is layered on after using the more relevant window and confidence ceiling.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Recurring food demand and the spread of packaged products give a plausible runway. The bottom-up capacity bridge is less secure: approximately 75% utilization is quoted in both recent years, but no reconciled annual tonnes, new throughput, unit realization, manufacturing contribution or channel sell-through accompanies the revenue doubling. Prospectus machinery utilization in FY24 was roughly 62.5-66.7%, rising to 75-78.3% in the September 2024 period, with differing machines/rates. These rates cannot be multiplied into a single invented company capacity.

The base model assumes 15% annual revenue growth,10.5% EBITDA margin and trade working capital declining from 62% to 52% of sales over FY27-FY32; capex is 2% of sales plus 2 crore assumed completion spending in FY27. This produces approximately 379.09 crore terminal TTM sales. Bull growth starts 25% and fades to 15%, margin 12%, ONWC improves 58% to 44%, and capex is 2.5%; bear starts flat, then 3-5% with 7.5% margin and heavier ONWC. These are stress paths, not management guidance. No unverified STK/Vandu/Haldiram opportunity is inserted as certain revenue.

A narrow incremental capital proxy uses trade ONWC plus PPE/intangibles/CWIP and EBIT after 30% tax. FY25-FY26 incremental NOPAT 3.20 on added capital 34.44 crore is 9.29%; FY24-FY25 is 6.60%, below the assumed 12-16% cost range. Yet incomplete other operating balances, comparative bridges and acquisition/control status prevent attributing these to a stable organic cohort. CAP stays NS, not automatically 3. Persistent cash weakness independently caps any otherwise complete GQS at 5. High sales growth with inventory and receivable reinvestment is not self-funding compounding.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The stewardship picture is mixed rather than an accusation. The IPO raised 25.116 crore gross; actual cash from equity 21.2725 and issue costs 3.8435 reconcile, versus estimated net 21.9539 in the prospectus. Planned objects were 15 crore working capital,4.25 branding and 2.7039 general purposes. No unverified unspent IPO amount is added to October cash. RPT sales 1.0885 and purchases 0.5785 crore total under 1% of revenue; the up-to 30 crore approval ceiling is not the same as actual transactions or a committed outflow. A notice-versus-note counterparty label needs correction. Management asserts arm's-length ordinary-course terms and a sole-agent rationale, which is preserved without independently validating pricing.

The October 16 board replaced the old 70 lakh warrants at 55 with 70 lakh at 60. It explicitly says no old warrants allotted and no cash received. Nine proposed allottees are described as public/non-related; reported floor 59.36 and valuation 53.45 are below issue price 60. Shareholder/BSE and other approvals remain conditions. Full exercise raises shares 39.12% but dilutes existing ownership 28.12%; those percentages are not interchangeable. A minimum 25% deposit is 10.5 crore, not 42 crore, and optional exercise of the balance is within 18 months.

Observable delivery includes real revenue/product expansion; capital allocation and integration are less clear. STK is 60% in overview text,51% in its table and 0.408 crore in investments, not consolidated. No primary completion/control bridge was located. CSR management disclosed nil FY26 spending due administrative evaluation and promised transfer by 30 September 2026; completed-transfer proof remains missing. Preserve this explanation alongside the inconsistent CARO wording. Neither unresolved disclosure nor a proposed raise is proof of abuse.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Read the main audit, CARO, IFC and audit-trail reports together. Main opinions and IFC are unmodified/adequate; audit trail is reported operated throughout, untampered and preserved. CARO reports no loan default or wilful default and no material going-concern uncertainty. Inventory NRV is a key audit matter. However CAROii(b) says quarterly bank returns agree, while note 33 shows December 2025 bank 96.6967 versus books 97.2537 crore and a stated valuation difference 0.5571; March 2026 was not submitted. June rounding is immaterial. CSR CARO says fully spent, whereas the notes/directors show 18.30 lakh unpaid and explain the planned delayed transfer. FY25 CSR spending descriptions also conflict. These specific reconciliations, not an assumed blanket audit failure, drive G2 Hold.

FY26 PBT 15.9965 plus finance 3.2572 and depreciation 1.0163 less other income 0.418 gives operating EBITDA 19.852. The cash-flow addback uses 2.9927 interest, excluding 0.2645 finance charges. Cash before working-capital movements 19.9259 becomes minus 6.3359 after inventory minus 23.6468, receivables minus 3.1840, payables minus 2.4889 and other net movements; cash tax 0.0989 takes CFO to minus 6.4348. Capex 6.2701 and financing-classified interest 2.9927 make owner cash after these uses minus 15.6976. Net borrowing 15.8069 and other investing items reconcile closing cash 0.1585 within 0.0001 rounding.

Receivables older than one year 15.52% versus 6.39% are more concerning than the faster sales denominator suggests. Management's insurance statement is not a proven cash guarantee. Tax payable 8.9253, CSR 0.183, capital creditor 0.5, gratuity 0.1192 and temporaryOD 4 must not disappear from valuation. Source-version differences are preserved, including the FY24 original finance cost 1.3658 versus restated 1.1427. The 0.01 subsidiary consolidation cash difference is normal scope, not misconduct. Note 51's broad balance-confirmation caveat requires follow-up. Full historical, original-version, debt, aging, cash and incremental-capital rows are embedded below and in the canonical.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At the qualified INR 60 reference, market value 107.35 crore, reported PE 10.19x, PB 1.45x and March net-debt EV/EBITDA 7.26x are arithmetic snapshots, not current transaction valuations. Prior-period tax charges 0.7798/0.7802 recur, so reported PAT is retained rather than automatically normalized upward. No separate property value is added to operating EV; restricted/unverified FD 0.0257, security deposits 1.0786 and disputed investments are not spendable cash. No NCI is invented for unconfirmed STK control.

The model starts 31 March 2026 and explicitly bridges to 20 October entry. Its required cash is the higher of 1 crore and 1% sales, an analytical buffer rather than a statutory minimum. Opening tax, CSR and capital creditor are assumed settled once in the conservative bridge. The proposed 0.50/share dividend is separately reserved before entry as a conservative timing assumption, not a verified approval or payment; cash credit renewal is assumed only to construct the stress, not proven available. Signed base entry cash is minus 18.11 crore and required reserve 1.89 crore. Peak bear/base/bull reserve gaps are 28.92/38.58/38.88 crore. All ordinary terminal prices, IRRs and hurdle entries remain null, including any apparently attractive non-rescue equity algebra. Negative cash is not relabelled debt capacity.

Separate counterfactual equity at 42,3% fees and repeated timely injections requires gross 29.82/39.78/40.08 crore, with holder dilution 28.41%/34.61%/34.78%. Hypothetical rescue terminal prices 22.67/90.66/191.20 imply minus 17.69%/8.61%/26.09% annual returns at 60. Base rescue-only hurdle entries are 51.45/45.08/39.63 at 12/15/18%, not ordinary buy levels. Full proposed warrants at 60 would change dilution and timing, so the 42-rupee rescue is not mislabeled the actual offer. Growth/multiple, margin/ONWC, interest, capex, impairment and obligation sensitivities are embedded. Reverse-expectation scans enforce valid brackets; no endpoint is reported as a solution. DCF is not forced onto an unresolved funding/perimeter base.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is that bulk dryfruit growth produces accounting spread but ties up cash faster than profits can replenish it. A combination of commodity-price correction, spoilage, slower customer collections, concentration, tighter bank eligibility or delayed optional warrant exercise can force equity funding at a worse price. This need not require fraud: normal credit losses and an unfavorable cash cycle can permanently dilute otherwise profitable owners.

The bear diagnostic holds initial sales flat, then grows 3-5%, cuts EBITDA margin to 7.5%, retains 70% initial ONWC and uses a 5 x exit multiple. Even with hypothetical rescue it ends near 22.67 per share, roughly 62% below 60; absent finance it is not a viable ordinary investment path. A simple accounting stress haircut of 10% receivables,20% inventory and 50% operating assets, plus advances/investment writeoffs, yields 26.39 per share;20%/30%/70% yields 17.93. These 56-70% discounts are not realizable liquidation floors, since timing, taxes, secured claims, recovery cost and marketability can worsen outcomes.

Countercase: FY26 cash burn improved markedly, retained spread rose, audited default findings are absent, and completed equity funding plus collections could repair the balance sheet. The thesis-break variable is collectible, bank-eligible working capital, not merely reported annual sales. Reconciliation of bank returns and ageing, insurance claim terms and cash receipts is therefore more useful than projecting a promotional addressable market. Downside risk is High, with uncertainty in shareholder recovery under adverse refinancing; no probability of bankruptcy is claimed.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold gains over five years require approximately 37.97% and 58.49% annual equity compounding. At 60 these mean 300 and 600 per share. Existing share count would require 536.74 and 1,073.49 crore equity values; full proposed warrants would raise those requirements to 746.74 and 1,493.49 crore before any further dilution. The model's bull terminal price is only 191.20 after its explicitly different rescue structure, despite substantial growth, margin improvement, working-capital compression and a 9 x multiple.

At a 9 x exit and 12% EBITDA margin, enterprise value scales at 1.08 times sales before net debt and required reserves. Achieving a fivefold share price would therefore require far greater funded sales/earnings than the base, or a substantially richer multiple, and a tenfold outcome would be still more demanding. No completed capacity/customer/collection/funding bridge supports those joint conditions today. These are feasibility hurdles, not upside targets or a claim that such outcomes are impossible. The relevant task is proving scalable cash generation and controlling dilution before extrapolating extreme share-price outcomes.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Cash and funding: obtain the next published cash/debt statement plus facility limits, renewal dates, eligible drawing power and temporaryOD settlement. Require a conservative obligations bridge that remains above the explicit operating reserve; a proposal or sanctioned limit without available headroom is insufficient.
2. Collections: track receivables 75.50 crore and over-one-year 11.71 crore. Warning: older balances grow faster than sales or insured claims remain unresolved; improvement needs actual receipts, not re-aging.
3. Inventory: track 57.10 crore, stock eligibility, physical verification, NRV/spoilage and stock-insurance coverage. Reconcile March bank submission and December 0.5571 crore valuation difference.
4. Earnings-to-cash: demand positive cumulative operating cash after financing-classified interest and maintenance capex across successive half-years; distinguish inventory release from repeatable conversion.
5. Mix: disclose tonnes/realization, processing versus trading, brand/channel contribution, gross retained spread and repeat sell-through. Watch EBITDA margin falling below 9% without compensating capital efficiency.
6. Capital projects/acquisitions: confirm STK ownership/control, cash paid/unpaid, consolidation date, counterparties, term loans and actual incremental revenue/returns; keep unverified pipeline out of forecasts.
7. Warrants: track shareholder/BSE approvals, allotment date, actual 25% deposits, exercise timing, proceeds use and issued-share reconciliation. No optional 75% cash until received.
8. Reliability/governance: reconcile CSR competing statements and transfer, comparative accounts, RPT counterparty names and balance confirmations. New adverse findings can change G1; clarification can clear G2.
9. Tradability: establish valid 20/60 BSE sessions, median/mean turnover, true no-trade days, spread, surveillance and lot restrictions before implementation.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Research classification is a high-growth food trading/processing/distribution special situation with persistent cash-conversion weakness and a potential capital raise, not a verified compounder. GOV 5, MOAT 4 and CAP NS fail the compounder evidence requirements independently of valuation. BQS/GQS/IAS are incomplete and must not be ranked against complete issuers. G2/G3/G4 remain Hold; G1 is Conditional rather than Fail because no substantiated integrity abuse was established and management explanations/counterevidence were retained.

Conditional action is monitor and resolve evidence, not an ordinary purchase recommendation at 60 or at any fabricated lower threshold. A lower share price cannot cure missing current financeability; the rescue-only 45.08 base 15% hurdle entry is explicitly not an investable buy level. A credible updated balance/obligation bridge, completed funding or collections, reconciled statutory schedules and verified trading data can reopen valuation. Better incremental capital evidence may permit CAP and quality composite scoring even before all implementation data are complete. Conversely, confirmed arrears, failed refinancing, material receivable losses or adverse control findings would strengthen downside concerns. This is analytical research, not personalized advice, an execution instruction or a guarantee.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary issuer annual reports and the final IPO prospectus supply the financial/business evidence; the October 16 underlying board filing governs the warrant status. Source locators use printed page numbers unless explicitly physical. Raw originals were examined locally, including the complete audit package and visual checks of the material contradictory tables. Dated secondary quote/history data are separately labelled and never override primary security identity. Undated peer business pages support qualitative economics only; historical peer financials come from the issuer prospectus and are not current multiples.

The canonical embeds annual historical data, original-version bridges, product revenue, actual cash reconciliation, annual and dated model rows, rescue mechanics, sensitivity matrices, reverse-bracket results, scoring and evidence. Model units are INR crore except per-share rupees, shares and liquidity rupees. CFO uses company classification; interest in financing is explicitly deducted for owner-cash comparison. Forecast taxes are 30% on positive current PBT, while opening tax liabilities settle separately once. ONWC is narrowly inventory plus receivables less payables; omitted/seasonal needs are stressed rather than hidden. No unspent IPO proceeds, optional warrant cash, restricted deposits or receivable releases are treated as established resources.

Open questions are the current public funding bridge, detailed bank reconciliation, CSR transfer, financial-comparative bridge, balance confirmations, STK/control and remaining commitments, customer collections/insurance, unit economics and verified BSE execution data. Post-cutoff reports, including a 21 October publication about a marketing arrangement, do not inform the 20 October assessment. Safe analytical backups retain public URLs and hashes plus paraphrased factual extracts, not original PDFs/OCR/shareholder lists. Reproduction verifies calculations and consistency; it does not freshly authenticate the omitted original documents.

evidence.claim: Exact issuer: Leo Dryfruits & Spices Trading Limited, INE0RH001011, BSE 544329, VANDU, CIN L10799MH2019PLC333102. Official master row shows 2,000-share lot and 17,891,440 shares.
evidence.locator: Cover, board letterhead, exact security row

evidence.claim: IPO-period FY24 sales were 77.17% trading and 22.83% processing; FY24 channels B 2 B 77.18%, B 2 C 16.99%, D 2 C 5.83%. FY24 Maharashtra 96.71%; top-ten customers 44.29%, increasing to 93.32% in H1FY25.
evidence.company_response_or_counterevidence: No long-term customer contracts; diversification strategy and APMC proximity are positives.
evidence.status: Historical, not extrapolated as FY26 mix

evidence.claim: Revenue grew from INR 36.4396 crore FY23 to 174.241 FY26, 68.47% three-year CAGR; gross retained spread grew 7.8630 to 30.2381, 56.67% CAGR. FY26 EBITDA margin compressed to 11.39% from 16.93%.
evidence.locator: FY26 notes 22-28 and prospectus restated financials
evidence.company_response_or_counterevidence: Growth in retained spread supports real economic scaling, but quantities, realization and organic/acquired contribution are not separately disclosed.

evidence.claim: FY26 dryfruit sales 73.8535 versus 9.235 crore, whole spices 73.7338 versus 71.3717, blended 10.174 versus.3413. Dryfruit addition accounts for 74.33% of total revenue increment.
evidence.company_response_or_counterevidence: New channels and product breadth may diversify dependence; product revenue is not brand-level contribution.

evidence.claim: FY22-FY26 cumulative CFO minus 62.9159 crore versus PAT 29.0532; FY24-FY26 CFO minus 52.0319 versus PAT 25.3396. CFO excludes financing-classified interest, so owner cash is weaker.
evidence.company_response_or_counterevidence: Working-capital investment accompanies growth and FY26 cash burn improved sharply; five consecutive negative years are not a single transient build.

evidence.claim: FY26 inventories 57.1022, debtors 75.4956 and creditors 24.8301 crore. Debtors older than one year 11.7142, 15.52%, versus 4.6280, 6.39%, in FY25; all shown good.
evidence.company_response_or_counterevidence: Management states debtors insured, but policy exclusions, insured limits, claims and recoveries are not independently established.

evidence.claim: At 31 March 2026 cash.1585 crore includes physical cash.1276 and bank.0309; debt 36.9467 includes cashcredit 29.1944, temporaryOD 4, current maturities.454 and LT 3.2983. Tax payable 8.9253, CSR.183, capital creditor.5.
evidence.company_response_or_counterevidence: CARO reports no default or wilful default and no material going-concern uncertainty; these are not proof of October cash/headroom.

evidence.claim: Main statutory opinions unmodified; separate IFC opinion adequate/effective; audit-trail reporting says operated throughout, not tampered and preserved. Inventory valuation is a key audit matter.
evidence.company_response_or_counterevidence: Clean audit conclusions explicitly retained; they do not erase contradictory detailed schedules.

evidence.claim: CAROii(b) says quarterly working-capital returns agree. Note 33 shows Dec bank/books 96.6967/97.2537 crore, reported valuation difference.5571, and March 2026 statement not submitted; June rounding difference is immaterial.
evidence.company_response_or_counterevidence: Management labels December a valuation difference. No full reconciliation or March submission proof by cutoff.
evidence.status: Unresolved reporting/control contradiction, not fraud finding

evidence.claim: CAROxx says CSR fully spent/no unspent. Note 36 shows 18.30 lakh required, nil expenditure and 18.30 shortfall; FY25 note shows 4.90 lakh shortfall although FY25 directors/annexure describe 10 lakh spending.
evidence.locator: FY26 printed 48,56-58,73,102,135 and FY25 CSR annexure
evidence.company_response_or_counterevidence: Directors disclose delay due administrative evaluation of suitable implementing projects and planned transfer by 30 September 2026. Proof of completed transfer by cutoff not found.
evidence.status: Competing reporting locations retained; delay explanation is evidence of disclosure, not concealment

evidence.claim: FY25 original CFO minus 30.879 crore becomes minus 31.0267 in FY26 comparative; original cash.2698 versus.2783 and assets 117.4234 versus 117.1683. FY24 prospectus restatement differs from original annual comparator PAT 6.6369/6.7294 and CFO minus 14.5704/minus 14.3766.
evidence.locator: Separate original_versions register with printed financial pages
evidence.company_response_or_counterevidence: General regrouping is disclosed, but no line-by-line bridge located. FY26 .01 standalone/consolidated cash difference is normal subsidiary scope, not an error.
evidence.status: Version differences preserved, no mechanical addition of unlike periods

evidence.claim: Note 51 says receivables/payables/borrowings/loans/advances/deposits subject to confirmation. RPT note identifies sales 1.0885 crore to J KetanKumar and purchases.5785 from V S Spices; notice attributes both to J KetanKumar.
evidence.company_response_or_counterevidence: Company says ordinary-course arm's-length, includes sole-agent rationale. Actual combined 1.667 crore differs from up-to 30 crore approval ceiling.
evidence.status: Counterparty-label clarification required; no evidenced diversion

evidence.claim: FY26 overview describes STK 60% in text and 51% in table; directors disclose.408 crore investment, carried as investment, not consolidated. Only Leo Catering is consolidated.
evidence.company_response_or_counterevidence: Subsidiary auditor Other Matter says nil assets/revenue; intercompany.01 elimination explains reported cash difference. Completion/control timing and any remaining STK commitments require evidence.
evidence.status: Material acquisition/perimeter ambiguity; unverified Vandu/Haldiram pipeline excluded

evidence.claim: 16 Oct 2026 board cancels prior 70 lakh warrants at 55; none allotted/no cash. New 70 lakh at 60 proposed for 42 crore, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals; minimum 25%10.5 crore then optional 31.5 within 18 months.
evidence.company_response_or_counterevidence: Nine public non-promoter, non-related-party allottees; issue price exceeds reported 59.36 floor and 53.45 valuation. Objects 36 WC/6 GCP.
evidence.status: Proposal, not received cash or full dilution already outstanding

evidence.claim: FY25 IPO gross 25.116 crore, actual equity cash 21.2725 and issue costs 3.8435. Planned net 21.9539 differed from actual; no verified unspent current proceeds. FY26 EPS 5.89 versus 5.75 despite 29.09% PAT growth.
evidence.locator: Equity, EPS, IPO objects, cash-flow tables
evidence.company_response_or_counterevidence: IPO expanded permanent capital and could fund scale. No hypothetical IPO addback; proposed 0.50/share dividend is conservatively reserved before entry, not verified paid and not counted as new-investor income.

evidence.claim: Dated secondary quotes agree INR 60 on 19 October with 40,000 volume. Verified official master lot 2,000; 19-row secondary history lacks complete 20/60 sessions and measured executable spread.
evidence.locator: Exact ISIN row and dated quote displays
evidence.company_response_or_counterevidence: Some secondary labels incorrectly call issuer NSE-listed; official/issuer identity takes precedence. Missing observations are not zero-trade sessions.
evidence.status: Quote usable only as qualified reference; L remains NS

evidence.claim: Model uses explicit October 2026/2031 boundaries, signed deficits, minimum cash, opening tax/capital creditor/CSR once, and no available equity or new debt. All ordinary returns/entries null; rescues are separate counterfactuals.
evidence.company_response_or_counterevidence: Hypothetical full 42 crore warrants could meet aggregate base gap at assumed fees, but deposit alone and timing cannot establish financeability.
evidence.status: Analytical assumptions, not company guidance or actual financing failure

evidence.claim: Peer economic contrasts: Proventus integrates bulk sourcing and brand/white label; Madhusudan spans spice products; Sarveshwar rice processing has different working-capital/export/aging economics. Prospectus historical peer margins differ materially.
evidence.company_response_or_counterevidence: No same-cutoff verified peer multiples claimed; old IPO comparisons are context, not rerating entitlement.
